measurementPolicy.meaning: Evidence-backed end-to-end readiness for a fully working, private, tested, hardened Remote Joining experience.
measurementPolicy.increaseRule: Increase only when new verified evidence materially improves an existing fixed capability domain.
measurementPolicy.decreaseRule: Decrease only when previously credited capability evidence is invalidated or a proven regression removes capability.
measurementPolicy.modelChangeRule: Changing domain weights or the denominator requires a new modelVersion, explicit rationale and backcast of prior comparable scores.
measurementPolicy.reportingRule: Every substantive owner-facing development checkpoint reports the latest calculated score even when it does not change.

domains.label: Deterministic sync and recovery safety
evidence: Deterministic revision/CAS/idempotency/tombstone contracts are proven.
Two-device/offline-reconnect harness proves stale conflict, replay, reconnect convergence and local-only fallback.
Candidate A/B/C recovery authority and canonical local storage safety remain protected.

domains.label: Identity, authentication, authorization and trust
evidence: Firebase Authentication provider decision and production Google sign-in configuration are proven.
Verified UID to accountId boundary, revocation-aware ID-token verification and operation-specific authorization contracts are proven.

2026-08-21 owner-supplied real mobile production evidence proves the Google popup sign-in flow completes against the production Firebase Auth project and returns a live authenticated Firebase identity in the installed application.
Stage 2I App Check verification order and trusted endpoint attestation contract are proven but production trusted runtime/IAM is not activated.

domains.label: Production cloud and security activation
evidence: Production Firebase project, Web App, Firestore database, restricted Browser API key, Google Auth and GitHub Pages authorized domain are provider verified.
Production Firestore Security Rules are provider verified through the strict authenticated self-account boundary and the later Stage 3 registered-device/private-pairing boundary.
2026-08-20 provider evidence proves reCAPTCHA Enterprise API/key setup and Firebase App Check Web App registration at one-hour TTL and 0.5 risk threshold with enforcement off.

Permanent Validate Stability Lane #1230 / run 32439162225 proves controlled production 1.4.0-r2 Firebase App + App Check runtime connection, exact-origin/path gating, every deployed runtime byte, and legitimate reCAPTCHA Enterprise App Check token traffic while enforcement remains off.
2026-08-21 owner-supplied real mobile production evidence proves the Connected Account surface, successful Google sign-in and strict self-account bootstrap path.
2026-08-21 owner-supplied production Stage 3 evidence proves the published zero-billing device/pairing Rules are exercised by the deployed v1.6.0-r1 browser path.
App Check enforcement and trusted-runtime IAM activation remain separately unproven and are not credited by this reconciliation.

domains.label: Devices, pairing, Connected Rivalry and actual Remote Joining
evidence: Remote schema and two-owner governance contracts reserve device, invite, session and rivalry identities.

Stage 3 is production-proven at v1.6.0 / 1.6.0-r1: two distinct authenticated browser device identities register successfully, a private one-use capability is created, wrong-slot redemption is rejected without changing local saves, and a distinct account successfully redeems into the required second manager identity.
The first live proof uses separate normal/incognito browser storage identities on one physical Chromebook; it proves two application device identities but not two-physical-machine hardening.

2026-08-24 live v1.7.0 / 1.7.0-r2 ordinary-browser evidence proves the first production Connected Rivalry slice: the exact private rivalry attaches under both entitled manager bindings, Player Two publishes the first authoritative shared gameplay projection at revision 0, and the distinct incognito Player One browser refreshes that same revision without local Apply or a reported local-save overwrite.

2026-08-24 owner-supplied evidence from a second independent production rivalry on iPhone proves an unrefreshed Player One publish cannot overwrite Player Two's newly created authoritative revision 0: the runtime rejects the stale base and reports that local saves were not changed.

The same iPhone production sequence then proves deterministic recovery and convergence: Player One refreshes after rejection to revision 0, publishes exactly once to monotonic revision 1, and Player Two refreshes that same revision 1 without local Apply or a reported local-save overwrite.
Exact idempotency replay, third-account/revoked-device negatives, two-network/adverse-network hardening, remote-to-local reconciliation and actual Remote Joining sessions remain uncredited.

domains.label: Real-device hardening and stable release
evidence: Existing browser-first/offline/recovery discipline and rollback architecture reduce downstream risk.

2026-08-24 owner-reported installed Career Mode app and Safari contexts on one physical iPhone exercise a second independent production rivalry through authorized refresh, revision-0 publication and stale-base rejection. This adds mobile cross-surface Connected Rivalry coverage.

2026-08-24 owner-supplied production evidence across one Chromebook and one iPhone proves fresh one-use pairing, revision-0 publication, live stale rejection, recovery and revision-1 convergence across two physical devices without local Apply or a reported local-save overwrite.
Remote Joining specific two-network/adverse-network and token-lifecycle testing, abuse hardening, production rollback proof and final stable Remote Joining release acceptance remain incomplete.

evidenceHistory.reason: Reconstructed the metric against a fixed end-to-end capability denominator after discovering earlier denominator drift between prerequisite completion and true Remote Joining readiness.
Owner provider screenshots prove production reCAPTCHA Enterprise and Firebase App Check registration for the real Web App with one-hour TTL, 0.5 risk threshold and enforcement still off.

Permanent push-triggered Stability Lane #1230 / run 32439162225 on exact production head 3d2ebefec683e0b3bf6b2beac08d54f1c3d9e516 proves two previously uncredited production capabilities: controlled Firebase App + App Check runtime connection and legitimate production App Check token traffic. The +2 is deliberately limited to those two newly proven fixed-domain capabilities; no points are awarded for PR count, green CI by itself, documentation, WEC/SLE work, App Check enforcement, trusted-runtime IAM, pairing, Connected Rivalry or actual Remote Joining.

Owner-supplied real mobile production evidence proves the installed application opens the production Google popup sign-in flow and returns to a live authenticated Firebase identity. This credits one previously unproven production authentication capability only.

Owner-supplied real mobile production evidence shows 'Private account ready'. Current source reaches that state only after the authenticated Firebase UID self-account bootstrap returns ok with active status, materially proving the bounded production Auth + memory-only Firestore + strict revision-0 self-account create path. No points are awarded for pairing, Connected Rivalry, actual Remote Joining, App Check enforcement or unactivated trusted-runtime IAM.

Owner-supplied live v1.6.0 / 1.6.0-r1 screenshots materially prove the first production Stage 3 capabilities: two distinct authenticated browser device identities register, a private one-use pairing capability is created, wrong-slot redemption is rejected without changing local saves, and a distinct account successfully redeems into the required second manager slot. The +6 is deliberately bounded to registered-device/private-pairing production capability. It does not credit emulator-only replay/third-account/revocation negatives, two-physical-machine hardening, Connected Rivalry, shared gameplay synchronization or actual Remote Joining.

Owner-supplied live v1.7.0 / 1.7.0-r2 ordinary-browser evidence proves three previously uncredited production capabilities within the fixed device/pairing/Connected-Rivalry/Remote-Join domain: each entitled manager binding can attach to the exact private rivalry, Player Two creates the first authoritative shared gameplay projection at revision 0, and the distinct incognito Player One browser reads that same revision without local Apply or a reported local-save overwrite. The +3 is deliberately limited to those three capabilities. It does not credit revision advancement, stale-base rejection, idempotency replay, third-account or revoked-device denial, two-physical-device hardening, remote-to-local reconciliation, or actual Remote Joining sessions.

Owner-supplied production evidence from a second private rivalry proves a stale Player One context cannot overwrite Player Two's newly created authoritative revision 0. The deployed runtime rejects the stale base, instructs refresh, and reports that local saves were not changed. The +1 is limited to live stale-base conflict protection; repeated attach, empty read and revision-0 publication receive no duplicate credit.

Owner reports the second rivalry proof was executed across the installed Career Mode app and Safari on one physical iPhone. Screenshots show distinct Player Two and Player One bindings, revision-0 publication and the corresponding stale-client rejection. The +1 credits bounded mobile cross-surface hardening only; it does not credit two-physical-device testing, revision advancement, stale recovery, final release acceptance or actual Remote Joining.

Owner-supplied production screenshots from the second iPhone rivalry prove three previously uncredited capabilities after a live stale-base rejection: Player One refreshes safely to the authoritative revision 0, publishes exactly once through the CAS update path to monotonic revision 1, and Player Two refreshes that same revision 1 without local Apply or a reported local-save overwrite. The +3 is limited to stale recovery, revision advancement and cross-manager convergence. It does not credit exact idempotency replay, negative authorization/revocation paths, two-physical-device hardening, remote-to-local reconciliation or actual Remote Joining.

Owner-supplied production evidence across a Chromebook and iPhone proves a fresh one-use pairing, exact Player One/Player Two attachment, revision-0 publication, cross-device observation, live stale-base rejection, recovery and revision-1 convergence across two physical devices without local Apply or a reported local-save overwrite. The +1 is deliberately limited to closing the previously uncredited two-physical-device boundary. It does not credit source work, release activity, two-network/adverse-network testing, token lifecycle, remote-to-local Apply or actual Remote Joining sessions.
